candidates.rationale: Persistently high asset profitability marks durable quality compounders that investors underprice while chasing glamour growth names, so the profitability premium reflects slow correction of this quality mispricing.

Sustained high equity profitability signals a durable competitive moat that slow-moving analyst coverage takes time to fully recognize, so persistently high-ROE firms earn a re-rating premium as coverage catches up.

A persistently elevated operating margin reveals real pricing power and cost discipline that generic sector discount rates fail to credit, so durable margin strength is underpriced relative to its lower cash-flow risk.

Profitability confirmed by high asset turnover indicates operating efficiency rather than an accounting or margin-only artifact, and this cross-statement confirmation is under-exploited because segmented analysts rarely combine both explicitly.

Scaling ROE by leverage isolates operating profitability from financial amplification; investors who extrapolate headline ROE without this adjustment overvalue leverage-driven returns and underprice equally profitable but safer firms.

Joint strength in both balance-sheet (ROA) and income-statement (margin) profitability is a more reliable quality signal than either metric alone since it is less sensitive to one-off items in a single statement.
Netting out the accrual component isolates the cash-backed portion of profitability; per the accrual anomaly, investors fixate on headline ROA and under-discount its less-persistent accrual portion.

A composite of high profitability, high margin, and low leverage proxies the quality-minus-junk construct; investor preference for lottery-like risky growth names causes systematic underpricing of boring, safe, profitable firms.

Lower financial leverage reduces distress and refinancing risk that investors habitually underweight during calm periods, so low-leverage firms trade cheap relative to their true risk, generating a persistent safety premium.

Generating more revenue per dollar of assets reflects a leaner, more scalable operating model whose efficiency is not a headline reported ratio, so the market is slow to connect current turnover strength to future margin gains.

Recency-weighting the margin level emphasizes the most current profitability trend before analysts have fully updated trailing multi-quarter averages, so the freshest margin information predicts drift as estimates catch up.

An exponentially smoothed ROE weights the latest reported profitability regime more heavily than older quarters, and because investors anchor on longer trailing averages, the freshest regime is underpriced until confirmed.

A firm sitting near the top of its own short-term profitability range signals a locally strengthening earnings regime that extrapolative analysts diagnose with a lag, so self-referenced strength predicts further upward revisions.

The product approximates the operating, non-financing component of return on assets; isolating operating-driven profitability from leverage-driven returns identifies sustainable earning power the market misprices when it skips this decomposition.

Margin earned per unit of asset turnover proxies pricing power independent of sales volume, and capital-light, high-margin business models are systematically under-rated by generic sector multiples that ignore this distinction.

A short-run rise in asset profitability is fresh fundamental news that analysts anchored on trailing estimates under-react to, so recently improving ROA predicts continued drift as post-earnings-announcement effects play out.

A recent jump in equity profitability signals either operating strength or a favorable capital-structure action that the market incorporates slowly, generating an earnings-momentum-style drift as later quarters confirm the change.

Short-run margin expansion from cost control or pricing gains is an early, visible sign of an operating inflection that leads revenue and earnings recognition in analyst models, so the freshest margin move is under-reacted to.

An ROA increase paired with falling leverage indicates profitability improvement that is self-funded rather than risk-financed, a distinction the market ignores when pricing raw profitability changes, so genuine quality gains are underappreciated.

Margin change that exceeds its own recent average pace signals accelerating, convex operating momentum rather than a one-off step, and analysts who extrapolate linearly systematically under-forecast accelerating fundamentals.

Scaling the margin change by its own recent volatility separates economically meaningful surprises from routine noise, analogous to standardized unexpected earnings, and large standardized surprises are known to be under-reacted to.

An improving ratio of sales to assets reflects an operational efficiency gain, such as working-capital or inventory improvement, that precedes its recognition in reported margins and ROA, so the market lags in pricing it.

A short-run rise in accruals signals more aggressive, less cash-backed earnings recognition, and per the accrual anomaly the market fails to fully discount this deteriorating earnings quality, so rising accruals precede weak returns.

Same-direction moves in both ROA and operating margin corroborate a genuine, broad-based profitability inflection rather than a one-off item in a single ratio, and this higher-conviction signal is priced more slowly than either metric alone.

Standardizing the short-run ROE change across the cross-section isolates firms with unusually large profitability moves relative to peers this period, and outsized relative surprises are under-reacted to, producing gradual re-rating drift.

The gap between the ROE change and the ROA change isolates the financing-driven portion of the profitability move; when ROE moves more than ROA, the improvement is leverage- rather than operations-driven, a distinction the market often misreads.

Scaling the raw EPS change by book value per share converts an absolute earnings surprise into a capital-scale-comparable surprise; unscaled EPS surprises are harder for investors to compare across firms, so the scaled surprise is priced with a lag.

A short-run rise in leverage often reflects debt-financed buybacks or acquisitions taken when managers view equity as overvalued, and the market underweights this financing-decision content, producing predictable underperformance after leverage jumps.

Repeated same-direction daily margin changes over the past week indicate a sustained operating inflection rather than an isolated accounting blip, and the market underweights persistence relative to single-day magnitude.

Weighting the recent profitability change by the firm's existing efficiency level highlights improvement at already-efficient, scalable operations rather than noisy improvement at inefficient firms, an interaction the market rarely combines explicitly.

Firms sustaining high asset turnover over a two-month window monetize their asset base efficiently, and because this slow-moving operating metric is underweighted relative to headline earnings, persistently efficient firms are underpriced and re-rate up as the efficiency shows up in results.

An exponentially-smoothed margin level reflects durable pricing power and cost discipline rather than a one-quarter blip, and analysts update long-run margin assumptions slowly, so high smoothed-margin firms keep outperforming as durability is confirmed.

This margin information-ratio rewards high average profitability relative to its own dispersion, and investors overweight generic volatility as risk while underpricing the quality premium that attaches to genuinely predictable margins.

Stable, not just high, asset turnover indicates a repeatable operating process rather than lumpy asset sales, and this lower operating-risk profile is underpriced relative to noisier peers with similar average turnover.

This approximates the operating-ROA component of the DuPont decomposition, and firms compounding high smoothed turnover and margin together are creating value from core operations rather than leverage, a quality distinction the market is slow to make.

This measures efficiency generated per unit of balance-sheet leverage, and firms that turn assets over quickly without relying on debt carry lower financial risk for a given operating profile, a safety premium the market does not fully price versus more levered peers.

This isolates asset profitability that is not simply a byproduct of financial leverage, and ROA earned by low-leverage firms is higher-quality and lower-risk than the same ROA levered up, a distinction investors initially underweight.

Standardized cross-sectional standing of smoothed margin level highlights structural cost or pricing advantages over the peer median, a durable competitive-advantage signal that diffuses into price only gradually.

Persistent positive co-movement between margin and turnover indicates a coherent, scalable operating model rather than a mechanical margin-volume trade-off, and this operating coherence is a genuine quality signal that neither metric captures alone.

Low or negative covariance between ROA and leverage over the medium run shows profitability is not being manufactured by rising debt, and ranking this deleveraged-profitability trait highlights sustainable earners the market conflates with more fragile, leverage-driven peers.

A recency-weighted efficiency level emphasizes the most recent operating quarters while still smoothing noise, flagging firms whose efficiency is improving into the present ahead of what a plain trailing average would show, capturing under-reaction to the latest trend.

Recency-weighted margin level surfaces currently strong and improving pricing power that a plain trailing mean would dilute with stale quarters, and the market anchors on that stale history and is slow to reprice the recent improvement.

This locates current margin within its own medium-run range, and firms operating near their trailing high are executing at peak effectiveness, a state the market under-extrapolates so it tends to persist a while longer than priced.

This scales smoothed margin by the magnitude of smoothed accrual aggressiveness, since margins backed by low accruals are cash-based and higher quality than equally-high margins propped up by aggressive accrual choices that the market pays for without adjusting.

Ranking firms inversely by smoothed margin volatility captures that erratic margins raise the discount rate investors apply for earnings unpredictability, so structurally stable-margin firms deserve a valuation premium the market under-applies in real time.

A positive recent change in asset turnover signals a genuine Piotroski-style improvement in operating efficiency, and because turnover updates diffuse into estimates slowly, recent improvers keep outperforming as later quarters confirm the trend.

Recent margin expansion reflects improving cost control or pricing power before it is fully reflected in trailing multiples, and analysts revise margin assumptions with a lag, producing sustained outperformance in recent margin-improvers.

An unusually high standardized turnover reading versus the firm's own recent distribution indicates a genuine operating step-change, such as a cost restructuring taking hold, that the market has not yet fully re-rated.

Flagging firms whose current margin sits far above their own recent normal range identifies structural improvement rather than noise, and standardizing lets the signal compare fairly across businesses with very different baseline margins.

A short-run rise in return on assets often precedes broader recognition of an earnings inflection, and because analysts anchor to trailing profitability, the improvement diffuses into estimates and price only gradually.

Netting the rank of recent ROE improvement against the rank of recent leverage increase isolates firms whose profitability is rising for reasons other than added financial leverage, a materially higher-quality and more persistent driver of ROE.

A sudden standardized spike in accrual gap versus a firm's own recent history flags fresh, aggressive earnings management, and such spikes historically precede disappointments and reversals as the unsustainable accrual component unwinds.

Scaling the recent efficiency change by the magnitude of recent leverage change isolates turnover gains achieved while the balance sheet is stable, which are more attributable to real operating improvement than efficiency changes that coincide with large financing-driven leverage swings.

Taking the weaker of the two recent changes means a high value requires both efficiency and profitability to have improved jointly over the past month, a more reliable Piotroski-style quality signal than either metric improving alone from a one-off mix shift.
Comparing very recent margin momentum to the broader medium-run change detects acceleration, an inflection the market has not yet extrapolated into estimates ahead of fuller recognition.

Scaling the recent margin change by the firm's own margin volatility produces a signal-to-noise-adjusted margin surprise akin to standardized unexpected earnings, so a large value reflects a statistically meaningful shift rather than routine quarter-to-quarter noise the market should discount less.

Scaling recent per-share book value growth by current profitability distinguishes organic, earnings-funded book value compounding from growth driven by dilutive issuance, and the former is a higher-quality, more persistent value driver the market under-recognizes at the balance-sheet update.

The gap between EPS-growth rank and operating-margin-growth rank isolates earnings growth not explained by core operating improvement, such as leverage, buybacks, or below-the-line items, and this non-operating-sourced growth is less persistent, so investors who extrapolate headline EPS are later disappointed.

A recent decline in accrual gap means reported income is converging toward cash flow, a shift toward more conservative, higher-quality accounting that the market treats as routine until it is confirmed in subsequent cash-flow statements, creating a window of underreaction.

Comparing very recent efficiency change against the broader medium-run change signals an accelerating improvement in asset utilization that analysts have not yet extrapolated into forward revenue-per-asset assumptions.

Firms with persistently high leverage carry structurally higher distress and financing-constraint risk that investors demand compensation for, a slow-moving risk-premium signal that shifts only as the long-run debt level itself changes.

Where current leverage sits within the firm's own trailing-year distribution reveals an unusually stretched or conservative capital-structure regime relative to its normal practice, which the market re-prices only gradually.

Exponentially smoothing leverage over nine months isolates the chronic, structural component of balance-sheet risk from one-off quarterly noise, proxying the persistent distress exposure that drives a long-horizon risk premium.

Standardizing the smoothed long-run leverage level across the cross-section flags structurally over-levered names independent of scale, capturing the persistent financing-constraint discount those firms carry.
Firms that combine chronically high leverage with chronically weak operating margins lack the cash-flow cushion to service debt, compounding distress risk beyond what either metric signals alone.

High leverage paired with high asset turnover indicates a firm using debt to aggressively scale revenue-generating assets, a levered-growth strategy whose latent risk the market underprices until conditions tighten.

Firms whose leverage swings widely over a multi-quarter window are pursuing unstable, opportunistic financing rather than a steady capital-structure policy, and that instability commands a higher uncertainty discount.

The direction of year-over-year leverage change separates firms actively re-levering, which the external-financing anomaly links to subsequent underperformance, from those de-levering toward improving credit quality.

Scaling the long-run leverage change by the firm's own average leverage level measures the relative size of a capital-structure shift, since a given debt increase matters far more for a historically low-leverage firm.

The trailing multi-quarter leverage growth rate captures the pace of debt-funded balance-sheet expansion; rapid growth is associated with subsequent negative abnormal returns per the external-financing literature.

Ranking the long-run leverage change against the firm's own recent history of such changes identifies episodes of unusually fast capital-structure deterioration, an acceleration signal beyond the change's raw magnitude.

Simultaneously rising leverage and falling operating margins signal a firm taking on more debt as its ability to service it from operations erodes, a two-statement deterioration the market digests slowly across separate filings.

Agreement in direction between the long-run leverage change and the long-run profitability change identifies the worst case, rising debt alongside falling returns on assets, as a compounded fundamental deterioration signal.

Recency-weighting the long-run leverage change emphasizes whether re-leveraging is accelerating in the most recent quarters, capturing momentum in credit deterioration that an endpoint-only delta would miss.

Persistently elevated accrual gap indicates earnings chronically supported by non-cash accounting components rather than realized cash flow, the classic low-quality-earnings condition that predicts negative returns as it unwinds.

A long exponential average of the accrual gap isolates the firm's structural reliance on accrual-based earnings from single-quarter noise, better identifying chronic earnings-management behavior than any one report.

Where the current accrual gap sits within the firm's own trailing-year range flags unusually aggressive accounting relative to that firm's normal practice, a within-firm earnings-quality deterioration signal.
Standardizing the chronic accrual level across all firms removes industry base-rate differences in accrual accounting, sharpening identification of genuinely extreme, low-quality-earnings names.

Scaling chronic accruals by the magnitude of long-run reported earnings measures how much of the earnings base is non-cash; a high ratio means profits are largely accounting constructs, raising reversal risk.

Normalizing chronic accrual generation by book value per share identifies firms building up non-cash earnings components that are large relative to their equity base, a scale-adjusted earnings-quality warning.

Firms combining high long-run reported profitability with high long-run accruals are more likely to have manufactured part of that profitability through accounting choices rather than cash generation.

High long-run volatility in the accrual gap reflects an inconsistent, opportunistic accounting policy rather than a stable one, and such inconsistency is associated with lower earnings persistence and restatement risk.
The direction of year-over-year change in the accrual gap separates firms newly ramping up aggressive accounting, deteriorating earnings quality, from those shifting back toward cash-backed earnings.

A sharp relative increase in accrual intensity versus the firm's own baseline signals a regime shift toward more aggressive earnings management, which the market unwinds slowly, generating the accrual anomaly's negative returns.

Ranking the long-run accrual-gap change against the firm's own recent history of such changes isolates unusually fast earnings-quality deterioration or improvement, an acceleration signal beyond the raw change.

Rising accruals are a stronger earnings-quality warning among firms already reporting cross-sectionally high ROE, since elevated accruals more likely inflate that reported profitability rather than reflect genuine returns.

The magnitude of year-over-year accrual-gap change, regardless of direction, proxies overall accounting-policy instability; large swings either way associate with lower earnings persistence and higher information risk.

The gap between a two-quarter and a full-year average accrual level captures an emerging shift in earnings-management intensity relative to the firm's own annual baseline, flagging new deterioration rather than chronic condition.

Simultaneous increases in both accrual intensity and leverage indicate a firm using aggressive accounting to mask rising financial risk, a compounded red flag that fragmented processing of filings lets the market miss.

A recent-to-long-run accrual ratio above one signals earnings quality deteriorating faster than the firm's historical norm, a leading indicator of accrual-anomaly overpricing before the eventual reversal.

Earnings scaled by book value per share is a price-free profitability-per-invested-capital measure distinct from accounting ROE; short smoothing filters report-date stamping noise so the cross-sectional rank captures a persistent capital-efficiency trait that analyst coverage prices in only gradually.

Exponentially smoothing the cross-sectional rank rather than the raw price-free earnings-to-book ratio prevents a few near-zero-book-value outliers from dominating the average while still tracking the persistent relative-profitability signal that slow-moving analyst revisions eventually price in.

Rewarding smoothed asset profitability only for firms with below-peer-average leverage isolates earnings quality that is not manufactured with financial leverage, so the safer subset is under-priced relative to its true risk-adjusted quality until the market recognizes the distinction.

Screening the price-free earnings-to-book yield to firms with below-average accrual levels favors cash-backed rather than accrual-heavy earnings, which are more persistent, so the accrual-clean high-yield subset drifts upward as subsequent reports confirm that persistence.

Taking the minimum of two independently smoothed profitability ranks rewards only firms strong on both asset efficiency and margin, screening out cases where one flattering ratio masks weakness elsewhere, a dual-strength distinction the market prices in with a lag.

Standardizing the most recent change in EPS approximates standardized unexpected earnings, and because investors are documented to underreact to the magnitude of earnings surprises, larger standardized surprises predict continued price drift over subsequent weeks.

A rising per-share return on book, scaled by a stable equity base rather than by price, isolates genuine profitability improvement from valuation noise, and because this fundamental is stamped discretely at report dates its freshest change captures quality news that price adjusts to only gradually.

An unusually sharp recent drop in leverage relative to peers, from debt paydown or an equity infusion, lowers default and dilution risk, but equity markets reprice improving credit quality slowly, so rapidly de-levering firms tend to see gradual upward re-rating.

An early expansion in operating margin typically precedes upward analyst estimate revisions because sell-side models adjust to fresh operating leverage with a lag, so ranking the freshest margin inflection captures improving earnings power before consensus catches up.

When profitability is improving its own level captures a compounding quality premium, but when profitability is deteriorating leverage becomes the more decision-relevant risk driver, so conditioning the reward on the direction of the recent ROE move follows the shifting source of return-relevant information.

Combining smoothed capital efficiency, margin, asset turnover, and inverted leverage into one standardized score captures profitability, operating efficiency, and balance-sheet safety jointly, and because no single accounting choice can move all four components at once this quality-minus-junk-style composite is harder to game and is re-rated only as each report confirms it.

Averaging the price-free earnings-to-book yield over roughly a quarter and a half smooths around individual report noise to capture the sustained level of per-share profitability, and persistently high book-yield firms are quality compounders the market re-rates gradually as successive reports confirm the level.

Rewarding the smoothed price-free earnings yield only for firms with below-average accrual levels combines cheap-on-book with cash-backed earnings, the combination least likely to be reversed by future write-downs, a joint condition the market underprices relative to its persistence.

Firms that generate more sales per dollar of assets while carrying less debt achieve growth without financial engineering, a combination of lower operating and financial risk that investors tend to underweight relative to headline growth metrics, producing gradual outperformance as the safety is recognized.

Ranking the current price-free earnings yield against its own trailing two-month range identifies firms whose per-share profitability just reached a local high, a self-referential improvement signal independent of the cross-section's overall yield level that analysts fold into estimates only gradually.

The change in EPS over about a month, scaled by book value per share to control for firm size, approximates a normalized earnings surprise, and because investors are shown to underreact to earnings news for months a larger scaled surprise predicts continued drift over the medium-term horizon.

A sharp increase in accruals relative to peers signals that reported earnings increasingly rely on non-cash, judgment-based items rather than cash flow, historically a leading indicator of earnings management and subsequent negative surprises, so inverting the standardized recent accrual change rewards improving earnings quality.

Profitability improvement signals genuine operating strength rather than leverage-fueled returns only when it coincides with falling leverage, so conditioning the standardized ROE surprise on a concurrent deleveraging trend isolates organic gains that the market takes a quarter or more to fully price in.

Low dispersion in the price-free earnings yield over the past two months indicates predictable per-share profitability that should command a lower uncertainty discount, and because that reduced uncertainty is confirmed only gradually as later reports validate the stability, ranking stability rewards the more trustworthy quality signal.

The sign of the medium-term change in operating margin acts as a switch for whether current asset profitability is likely to persist or mean-revert, so multiplying that trend-direction flag by the profitability rank rewards firms both currently profitable and on an improving margin trajectory, a combination that has historically preceded further earnings beats.

Averaging profitability, margin, leverage, and accrual level over roughly three quarters isolates the structurally persistent component of a quality-minus-junk characteristic from quarter-to-quarter noise, and because such composites are shown to be underpriced the long-smoothed score forecasts returns over a multi-quarter horizon as the mispricing corrects.

Summing the accrual gap over a full trailing year aggregates four quarters into one robust measure of how much reported earnings rely on non-cash accounting items, and firms with the largest cumulative accrual burden have historically delivered the weakest long-horizon returns as the accruals reverse, so inverting the rank rewards low cumulative-accrual firms.

The gap between current profitability and its own trailing-year low captures the magnitude of an operational turnaround, and analysts anchor estimates to recently depressed earnings and revise upward only gradually, so firms furthest above their own trough tend to keep beating a still-conservative consensus.

Counting the periods over the trailing year in which asset profitability was positive measures the consistency, not just the average level, of earnings, and firms reliably profitable every quarter carry materially lower earnings-management and going-concern risk than sporadically profitable firms with the same average ROA, a distinction the market underweights.

When asset profitability rises and falls together with asset turnover over time, earnings improvements are driven by genuine sales-volume and efficiency gains rather than transient pricing effects, and this real source of profitability is more durable and cash-flow backed than the market credits within only a few quarters.

A large standardized shift in leverage over roughly two quarters reflects a structural capital-structure change such as a major refinancing, debt-funded buyback, or deleveraging, and because rating agencies and equity analysts reassess capital-structure risk with a lag, firms whose leverage has structurally declined are under-recognized as safer until risk premia catch up.

When quarter-over-quarter earnings growth and book-value-per-share growth move together over time, retained profits are directly building equity rather than being paid out, borrowed against, or diluted away, signaling an internally financed, sustainable growth rate that carries lower financing risk than the market re-rates only slowly.

A firm sitting at or near its own trailing-year peak accrual level is displaying the most aggressive non-cash earnings recognition it has shown all year, historically a red flag for subsequent negative surprises and write-downs, so ranking firms by how far current accruals sit below their own recent peak rewards more conservative, less-manipulated earnings.

Over a multi-quarter horizon, firms with genuinely improving profitability should be rewarded for margin strength reflecting durable pricing power, while firms whose profitability has been trending down for roughly two quarters are better characterized by their financial risk, so rotating the rewarded dimension follows the trajectory the market is slow to update on.

Firms whose return on equity has been stable over the past year carry less earnings-related uncertainty than firms with equally high but erratic ROE, and because quality research shows the market does not fully price low fundamental volatility as a risk-reducing trait, standardized ROE stability predicts a persistent long-horizon premium.

When a stock's 5-day ROA improvement outranks its own 5-day price move, the market has underreacted to the profitability jump (post-earnings-announcement drift), so price should keep drifting up to close that gap.

An ROA improvement paired with rising trading dollar-volume rank shows real capital already accumulating on the news, consistent with informed flow that keeps pushing price as the improvement diffuses rather than a signal nobody is acting on.

Efficiency gains that coincide with a positive very-recent return show technical and fundamental signals already agreeing, and agreement between two independent channels lowers the odds either is noise, favoring continuation.

ROE improving while the stock's own trading-attention percentile stays low means the gain is happening under limited investor attention, which delays incorporation and sets up a later re-rating once attention catches up.

A large ROA surprise relative to how much the stock's price is currently moving means daily price variance has not yet absorbed the news, so a high surprise-to-motion ratio flags a repricing that is still ahead of it.

When turnover is improving and return and volume are tightly co-moving (directional flow, not choppy noise trading), the price action looks informed, reinforcing that the efficiency gain is already being traded on with conviction.

A volume spike is more likely to reflect genuine new information, not speculative churn, when it occurs in an already-high-ROA name the market trusts, so quality conditions how reliable an attention shock is.

ROE rising faster than operating margin means the gain is leverage- or turnover-driven rather than core profitability, so a price rally that has already rewarded this lower-quality improvement is priced for a durability it likely doesn't have.

The same efficiency improvement gets arbitraged faster in liquid, high-dollar-volume names because capital can act on it without moving the price much, so turnover gains should convert into returns sooner where trading interest already concentrates.

Margin improving while the fast-versus-slow price-trend spread is still flat shows the market hasn't started trending the stock on the news yet; once a short-term uptrend forms on top of already-improving fundamentals, the two compound into continuation.

Pairing an ROE improvement with a price low that was touched very recently catches cases where the market sold the stock down hardest just as fundamentals turned, a setup where mean-reversion and improving quality reinforce rather than fight each other.

Weighting the turnover delta toward its most recent days isolates accelerating, not stale, efficiency gains, and when that acceleration coincides with elevated relative volume it marks the early stage of price discovery where most of the move is still ahead.

A high count of up-days rather than one large move suggests steady, low-volatility accumulation; paired with a genuine ROE improvement it looks like patient, informed buying, which tends to persist longer than a single speculative spike.

Standardizing both the fundamental surprise and the trading-activity surprise cross-sectionally puts them on comparable scales, so their product isolates a genuinely unusual joint move rather than being dominated by whichever series has fatter tails that day.

When margin is higher than it was three weeks ago recent momentum is left to run, since momentum in improving-quality names tends to be genuine; when margin is deteriorating the same recent return is inverted, because a rally into worsening fundamentals looks more like a technical bounce that mean-reverts.

Over a full quarter, ROE that has risen more than cumulative price has means the market has structurally under-priced the sustained profitability gain, the multi-week analogue of post-earnings drift, so return should keep drifting toward the fundamental.

A sustained efficiency improvement matters more when the stock currently sits at an unusually high percentile of its own recent trading activity, since that is when new information is most likely to actually be getting impounded into price rather than sitting ignored.

An ROA improvement alongside a rising volume trend suggests broadening participation and accumulation consistent with the better fundamentals, whereas the same improvement on shrinking volume signals skepticism that is more likely to fade than confirm.

Margin expanding over the past couple of months while the stock still sits near the bottom of its own trailing price range signals that price hasn't caught up to the improved profitability yet, a lagged-recognition setup that should close as the market re-rates the name.

The raw product of a medium-term ROA change and the concurrent cumulative return measures how much of the fundamental surprise the market has already started pricing and in which direction; a large same-signed product indicates real information-driven repricing already underway, which tends to have follow-through as full price discovery completes.

When a stock's best single-day return of the past month happened very recently at the same time asset turnover has been improving, the price move looks like it is catching up to a real efficiency gain rather than a stale, already-faded spike, favoring continuation.

A rising medium-term price-trend spread emerging on top of a sustained ROE improvement indicates the market is only now beginning to trend the stock in line with fundamentals already in place, an early-continuation signal rather than an already fully priced fact.

Counting how many of the last 20 days had higher volume than a month before measures a durable build in trading engagement rather than a one-off spike; paired with sustained margin improvement it signals a more lasting increase in investor interest backing the fundamental story.

Standardized alignment between a sustained ROA improvement and the cumulative two-month return rewards names where both channels already agree in the same direction, since concurrent fundamental-and-price confirmation over that long a window is a lower-false-positive continuation signal than either series alone.

Taking the minimum of the fundamental-improvement rank and the price-strength rank requires both conditions to hold simultaneously; this conjunctive gate screens out cases where only one channel looks good, which tend to be noisier and less persistent than genuine two-channel confirmation.

Squaring the peer-relative margin surprise emphasizes unusually large changes nonlinearly, consistent with markets reacting disproportionately to bigger surprises, while the sign of the trading-activity trend supplies the direction that magnitude alone cannot.

Capping the return-confirmation term keeps a single already-extreme price move from dominating the score by itself, anchoring the factor to the fundamental change for normal-range price action instead of degenerating into a pure momentum bet exactly where momentum crashes are most likely.

Compounding daily returns geometrically rather than summing them captures the true cumulative price effect including volatility drag, so pairing its rank with a turnover-improvement rank rewards efficiency gains that have genuinely compounded into higher realized performance over the month.

Taking the maximum of the margin-improvement rank and the price-strength rank catches names where at least one channel is already flashing strongly, since early-stage re-ratings often show up in one channel well before the other confirms, trading some false positives for earlier detection than a conjunctive gate would allow.

Pairing a genuine efficiency-driven improvement with an already-solid overall ROE level and current relative volume targets the more durable, harder-to-manufacture flavor of quality gain, with volume flagging that the market has actually started paying attention to it.

High financial leverage mechanically amplifies how operating cash-flow shocks translate into equity volatility, so heavy leverage combined with elevated realized volatility carries under-priced distress risk that resolves as negative drift.

Ranking leverage alongside the dispersion of the daily high-to-low ratio isolates firms whose capital-structure risk is compounding with genuine intraday trading uncertainty, a joint condition markets are slow to re-price into the discount rate.

A quarter-over-quarter rise in leverage that coincides with abnormally high recent trading volume suggests informed participants are already reacting to balance-sheet deterioration, and full price adjustment lags this early volume signal.

When high accruals (aggressive, low-quality earnings) coincide with a strong positive return-volume relationship, recent price gains look flow-driven rather than fundamentals-driven, setting up the classic accrual-anomaly reversal once quality concerns surface.

Downside-only return dispersion is the volatility component most relevant to default risk, so its interaction with leverage captures compounding solvency risk that symmetric volatility measures understate and that markets under-price.

A deteriorating accrual gap alongside a short-term expansion in volume dispersion relative to its longer-run level signals informed traders stepping up activity ahead of a quality-driven correction the broader market has not yet impounded.

A shrinking ratio of recent to trailing dollar volume signals fading market liquidity, which is disproportionately dangerous for highly levered firms that may need to raise capital or unwind positions, flagging amplified hard-to-exit risk.

Persistently wide intraday trading ranges reflect difficulty pricing a firm's fundamentals; paired with a high accrual gap this uncertainty is more likely rooted in genuine earnings-quality ambiguity, predicting negative returns as it resolves unfavorably.

A tight link between volume spikes and range expansion indicates a disorderly, liquidity-driven price-discovery regime; highly levered firms are more exposed to forced-selling cascades in such regimes, raising crash risk.

Margin compression signals eroding competitive position; when concurrent price moves are heavily volume-confirmed the market is actively but likely incompletely repricing this weakness, implying continuation as discovery catches up.

Declining asset turnover reflects deteriorating capital efficiency; the more liquid and closely watched a stock is, the more reliably this operational deterioration gets impounded into price with a short lag.

Rising volatility-of-volatility signals an unstable risk regime where refinancing terms and covenant risk are most sensitive; highly levered firms suffer disproportionately when the volatility regime itself turns erratic, a tail-risk premium level volatility alone misses.

A structurally elevated, full-cycle volatility regime combined with sustained high leverage indicates a persistently fragile capital structure whose distress risk the market prices in only gradually over long horizons.

A full year of rising leverage that is now drawing unusually high relative trading interest suggests the market is beginning, but has not finished, digesting a structural deterioration in balance-sheet risk.

Chronically aggressive accounting paired with a structurally elevated downside-volatility regime over two quarters suggests repeated negative surprises consistent with poor earnings quality, a slow-forming pattern that continues to unwind.

A sustained, multi-month widening of intraday trading ranges signals a structural rise in valuation uncertainty; since levered equity behaves like a call option on volatile assets, this compounds solvency-linked mispricing risk.
